subject: Orpheus preflight: on-prem k8s cluster, node pools & storage alignment
messages:

Cc: Claire Huang <claire.h@orpheus.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Preflight - Orpheus private deployment kickoff

Jordan — thanks again for the pre-kickoff yesterday. Claire and I pulled together the hardware inventory and a few constraints that will drive node and storage choices. High level: 3 racks (prod), dual spine leaf, on-site CEPH available for block, and one SAN we can use for model artifacts.

Questions we want to lock down in the workshop:
- Recommended control-plane HA sizing and whether we should run masters on dedicated VMs or as static pods on infra nodes
- Nodepool separation policy: we want isolation between inference-serving, batch-training, and infra services
- PV strategy: Rook/Ceph for persistent volumes vs mounting SAN for large model artifacts; are local NVMe caches required?
- Networking: CNI options (we run Calico in other clusters), MetalLB vs on-prem LB, and egress breakout suggestions
- Backups & snapshots (RBD snapshots or filesystem-level backups) and RPO expectations

Attached is the inventory and a quick IOPS matrix. Can we run a 60-minute workshop next week?

—Samir
Infra Lead, Orpheus Analytics

From: laura_bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.inference.com>
To: Samir Rao <samir@orpheus.ai>, Claire Huang <claire.h@orpheus.ai>, jordan_blake <jordan.blake@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.inference.com>, priyom_das <priyom.das@redwood.inference.com>, dev_patel <dev.patel@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 11:00:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Preflight - Orpheus private deployment kickoff

Thanks everyone — good session. Notes and recommendations below (summarized):

Control plane
- Recommendation: 3 control-plane nodes (separate VMs) behind an HA keepalived pair or VRRP; do not schedule inference workloads on masters.
- Resources: each control node 8 vCPU / 32 GiB for our expected scale (cluster ~120 nodes).

Node pools (recommended separation)
- infra-pool: 3–5 m5d-like VMs for logging/monitoring/csi/rook daemons (tainted as infra=true:NoSchedule).
- cpu-serves: xlarge machines (16 vCPU / 64 GiB) for API-serving, autoscale 4–12.
- gpu-inference: dedicated GPU servers (NVIDIA A30/A100 depending on models). Start with 4 GPUs, plan capacity for burst to 12. Use node-level GPU isolation and pod- level resource requests.
- batch/training: separate autoscaling group with larger ephemeral storage; spot-preemptible ok for non-latent jobs.

Storage strategy
- Persistent volumes: Rook/Ceph (RBD) for small persistent state (prometheus, postgres, etc.).
- Model artifacts: mount SAN (NFS) for cold model storage; copy-on-demand to local NVMe cache on gpu-inference nodes for low-latency serving.
- Local NVMe: required as L2 cache for models and KV cache; recommend at least 1–2 TB NVMe per GPU node.
- Backups: RBD snapshots nightly for critical PVs with weekly replication to off-site (we can propose solutions for snapshot tooling).

Networking & Load balancing
- CNI: Calico in policy-only mode is fine; recommend eBPF dataplane if available for perf.
- MetalLB for on-prem LBs; place MetalLB speakers in infra-pool with BGP if fabric supports it, fallback to layer2 mode.
- CIDR plan: cluster pod CIDR 10.244.0.0/16, service CIDR 10.96.0.0/12; reserve 172.20.0.0/16 for infra services.
- Egress: use NAT gateways per rack with centralized egress monitoring; allow model telemetry endpoints and Redwood telemetry endpoints (we'll provide IP ranges).

Operational notes
- Node eviction and disk-pressure: ensure kubelet eviction thresholds set and local NVMe used for cache only (not for PVCs unless configured with local-volume-provisioner).
- Monitoring: include node-exporter, cAdvisor, blackbox for model endpoints, and an alert for NVMe wear and high write amplification.
- Security: recommend mTLS between control plane components, KMS integration for disk encryption (we support HSM/KMS integrations in Private deployments).

Action items
- Redwood: provide a template for NVMe cache init scripts and RBD snapshot playbook (owners: laura_bennett, priyom_das).
- Orpheus: send exact rack-level NIC topology and SAN throughput numbers (owner: Samir).
- Follow-up: schedule design handoff week of 6/23 for implementation BOM and runbook.

—Laura Bennett
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Preflight - Orpheus private deployment kickoff

Thanks Laura — that level of detail is exactly what we needed. A few clarifications:
- For MetalLB BGP: our network team prefers BGP to avoid hairpinning; we'll provide ASNs and neighbor addresses.
- NVMe sizing: 1–2 TB per GPU node is okay as a starting point.
- Backup cadence: nightly snapshots are fine, but we need retention policy details. Can Redwood recommend retention defaults and snapshot retention tooling?

We'll send rack NIC diagrams and SAN throughput later today. Please include any recommended IaC snippets for Ceph/Rook (we run Terraform + Ansible currently).

—Samir

Subject: Re: Preflight - Orpheus private deployment kickoff

Samir/Claire — following up with deliverables as discussed. Attached: a short runbook snippet for NVMe cache initialization, a Ceph RBD retention recommendation (7 days incremental, 30 days archive by default), and a MetalLB BGP config template.

Key calls-outs:
- Snapshot retention: default 7-day incremental + 30-day weekly archive; we recommend adding offsite weekly exports for compliance. We can adjust per regulation.
- IaC: we’ll share Terraform modules for Rook operator and an Ansible role that sets up NVMe cache mountpoints and eviction guards.
- Next steps: sync 6/24 for BOM and rollout schedule.

Regards,
Priyom Das
Infrastructure PM, Redwood Inference
